input: What are the symptoms of Roseola?
chosen:
Roseola has two stages: fever and rash.
The first stage lasts for 3-4 days during which there will be high temperature (fever) but no other symptoms such as sore throat or coughing. The second stage also lasts about three to four days in which you have red spots on your skin. These rashes usually appear after the fever disappears. In some cases, these rashes may not show up at all. There might be itching sensation when the rash appears. However, it's rare.
In children, roseola can cause seizures due to febrile convulsions. This happens because their brains are still developing. Adults do not experience seizures from roseola.
There are different types of roseola. Some people get infected by herpes virus while others get infected by human herpesvirus 6. People who contract roseola through contact with someone else are more likely to develop complications like pneumonia, meningitis, encephalitis, etc.
People who suffer from weakened immune system should take precautions against getting infected with roseola. They could avoid close contact with anyone suffering from roseola. If they must come into contact with someone having roseola, make sure to wear protective clothing and wash hands frequently.
